-- Enable Row Level Security on all tables
alter table public.teams enable row level security;
alter table public.team_members enable row level security;
alter table public.documents enable row level security;

-- Helper function to check if current user is an editor in the target team
create or replace function public.is_team_editor(team_id bigint, user_id uuid)
returns boolean
language sql stable
security invoker
as $$
  select exists (
    select 1 from public.team_members
    where team_members.team_id = team_id
    and team_members.user_id = user_id
    and team_members.role = 'editor'
  );
$$;

-- Helper function to check if current user is a viewer in the target team
create or replace function public.is_team_viewer(team_id bigint, user_id uuid)
returns boolean
language sql stable
security invoker
as $$
  select exists (
    select 1 from public.team_members
    where team_members.team_id = team_id
    and team_members.user_id = user_id
    and team_members.role = 'viewer'
  );
$$;

-- R1: Users can see the teams they belong to.
create policy "Users can view teams they belong to"
on public.teams
for select
using (
  exists (
    select 1 from public.team_members
    where team_members.team_id = public.teams.id
    and team_members.user_id = auth.uid()
  )
);

-- R2: Users can see their own membership rows, not others'.
create policy "Users can view their own team memberships"
on public.team_members
for select
using (user_id = auth.uid());

-- R3: Members of a team can read team documents (editable by editors).
create policy "Team members can read team documents"
on public.documents
for select
using (
  (exists (
    select 1 from public.team_members
    where team_members.team_id = documents.team_id
    and team_members.user_id = auth.uid()
  ))
  and documents.deleted_at is null
);

-- R4: Editors can create documents; Viewers cannot.
create policy "Editors can create documents in their teams"
on public.documents
for insert
with check (
  exists (
    select 1 from public.team_members
    where team_members.team_id = documents.team_id
    and team_members.user_id = auth.uid()
    and team_members.role = 'editor'
  )
);

-- R5: Editors can edit any document in their teams (must still be editor after).
create policy "Editors can update documents in their teams"
on public.documents
for update
using (
  exists (
    select 1 from public.team_members
    where team_members.team_id = documents.team_id
    and team_members.user_id = auth.uid()
    and team_members.role = 'editor'
  )
  and documents.deleted_at is null
);

-- R6: Only the creator can delete (soft delete via deleted_at) a document.
create policy "Only document creator can soft delete"
on public.documents
for update
using (
  auth.uid() = created_by
  and documents.deleted_at is null
);

-- R7: Teams and memberships cannot be modified by users (deny insert/update/delete for anon/authenticated except service_role).
-- Since we want to allow service_role to bypass, we rely on the default deny for authenticated users on these tables.
-- Explicitly denying insert/update/delete for team_members and teams for authenticated users ensures no user changes.
create policy "Deny users from modifying teams"
on public.teams
for all
to authenticated
using (false);

create policy "Deny users from modifying team_members"
on public.team_members
for all
to authenticated
using (false);

-- R8: Anonymous visitors cannot see or change anything.
-- Policies above default to authenticated users where possible (e.g., R1, R2, R3 use auth.uid() or auth.jwt() context implicitly via row access).
-- Explicitly deny anon on all tables to be safe and clear.
create policy "Deny anonymous access to teams"
on public.teams
to anon
using (false) with check (false);

create policy "Deny anonymous access to team_members"
on public.team_members
to anon
using (false) with check (false);

create policy "Deny anonymous access to documents"
on public.documents
to anon
using (false) with check (false);

-- R9: Service role keeps full access.
-- By default, service_role bypasses RLS. No explicit policy needed for service_role to write, 
-- but we ensure they can read everything if policies restrict 'to authenticated'.
-- The policies above use 'to authenticated' or default behavior. 
-- To ensure service_role can do everything regardless of 'to authenticated' restrictions, 
-- we explicitly grant all to service_role on all tables.
grant select, insert, update, delete on all tables in schema public to service_role;

-- Ensure service_role can access the helper functions if needed (though they are invoker, so it depends on the user calling them, 
-- but service_role bypasses RLS on the tables, so if helper functions are used in policies, they run as the policy owner or user.
-- Since policies are evaluated per request, and service_role bypasses RLS, the policies effectively don't block service_role.
-- However, to be explicit and clean:
grant execute on function public.is_team_editor to service_role;
grant execute on function public.is_team_viewer to service_role;

-- Enable RLS on all tables
alter table public.finance_staff enable row level security;
alter table public.invoices enable row level security;

-- Helper function to check if user is finance staff
create or replace function public.is_finance_staff()
returns boolean
language sql
security definer
set search_path = public
as $$
  select exists (select 1 from public.finance_staff where user_id = auth.uid());
$$;

-- Helper function to check if user is the creator of the invoice
create or replace function public.is_invoice_creator()
returns boolean
language sql
security definer
set search_path = public
as $$
  select created_by = auth.uid() from invoices where invoices.id = raw.row_id;
$$;

-- Helper function to check if invoice is a draft
create or replace function public.is_draft_invoice()
returns boolean
language sql
security definer
set search_path = public
as $$
  select status = 'draft' from invoices where invoices.id = raw.row_id;
$$;

-- Helper function to check if user can modify customer/amount
create or replace function public.can_modify_customer_amount()
returns boolean
language sql
security definer
set search_path = public
as $$
  select 
    is_finance_staff() 
    or (is_invoice_creator() and is_draft_invoice());
$$;

-- Helper function to check if user can change status
create or replace function public.can_change_status()
returns boolean
language sql
security definer
set search_path = public
as $$
  select 
    is_finance_staff() 
    or (is_invoice_creator() and is_draft_invoice());
$$;

-- Helper function to check if user can delete invoice
create or replace function public.can_delete_invoice()
returns boolean
language sql
security definer
set search_path = public
as $$
  select is_invoice_creator() and is_draft_invoice();
$$;

-- Policy R1: Read invoices
create policy "Users can read invoices they created"
on public.invoices for select
using (auth.uid() = created_by);

create policy "Finance staff can read all invoices"
on public.invoices for select
using (public.is_finance_staff());

-- Policy R2: Create invoices
create policy "Users can create invoices as themselves as drafts"
on public.invoices for insert
with check (
  auth.uid() = created_by 
  and status = 'draft'
);

-- Policy R3: Update invoices (customer, amount, status)
create policy "Users can update invoices based on role and status"
on public.invoices for update
using (
  -- Finance staff can update anything
  public.is_finance_staff()
  -- OR Creator of draft can update customer, amount, and status (draft->sent)
  or (
    public.is_invoice_creator() 
    and public.is_draft_invoice()
  )
);

-- Policy R4: Specific status changes for sent invoices (only finance staff)
-- This is handled by the update policy above, but we need to ensure the logic is strict.
-- The update policy above allows finance staff to change status on any invoice.
-- It allows creators to change status ONLY if it is a draft.
-- This satisfies R4: "Finance staff can change a sent invoice's status... No other status change allowed".
-- If a creator tries to change a non-draft status, the `is_draft_invoice()` check fails, blocking them.

-- Policy R5: Delete invoices
create policy "Users can delete their own draft invoices"
on public.invoices for delete
using (public.can_delete_invoice());

-- Policy R6: Nobody can change who created an invoice
-- This is enforced by the INSERT policy (R2) which sets created_by to auth.uid() (default) or requires it to be the current user.
-- The UPDATE policy does not allow setting created_by because the USING clause doesn't check for it, 
-- but the security definer functions don't restrict column updates directly.
-- We need a check constraint or a more granular update policy.
-- Since we cannot modify existing tables, we rely on the fact that the INSERT policy defaults to auth.uid() and 
-- the UPDATE policy doesn't explicitly allow setting created_by. However, RLS doesn't prevent setting a column 
-- unless we use a check policy or the column is not updatable.
-- To strictly enforce R6 without altering the table schema, we can add a check policy on updates.
create policy "Prevent changing created_by on update"
on public.invoices for update
to authenticated
using (created_by = auth.uid());
-- Note: The above policy is redundant if the user is already authenticated and the logic holds, 
-- but it explicitly blocks any attempt to update the created_by column to a different value.
-- Actually, standard RLS update policies apply to the whole row. If we want to allow updates to other columns 
-- but block updates to created_by, we need to be careful.
-- The previous update policy allows finance staff to update everything. We need to restrict them too on created_by.
-- Let's refine the update policy to explicitly exclude created_by updates for non-authors, 
-- but since we can't use column-level restrictions easily in a single policy without complex logic,
-- we rely on the fact that the application shouldn't send it, and RLS doesn't block setting a column 
-- to the same value.
-- To strictly block changing created_by to a DIFFERENT value:
-- We can't easily do this in a single policy without checking the old value vs new value which isn't available in standard RLS.
-- However, the requirement says "Nobody can change who created an invoice".
-- If the app sends `created_by: 'other_user'`, we need to block it.
-- We can add a check policy that runs on INSERT and UPDATE.
create policy "Enforce created_by integrity"
on public.invoices for all
to authenticated
using (created_by = auth.uid());
-- This policy will block any user from inserting or updating the row if the created_by is not their own.
-- This effectively blocks Finance Staff from changing created_by as well, which is correct per R6.
-- But wait, Finance Staff need to update other fields. This policy blocks ALL updates if created_by != auth.uid().
-- This is too restrictive for Finance Staff who need to update status on sent invoices.
-- We need to allow Finance Staff to update the row, but NOT the created_by column.
-- Since we can't do column-level RLS easily, we assume the application logic prevents sending created_by.
-- OR, we can use a trigger to enforce it.
-- Let's use a trigger to enforce R6 strictly.

-- Trigger to enforce R6 (created_by cannot be changed)
create or replace function public.enforce_created_by()
returns trigger
language plpgsql
security definer
as $$
begin
  if (tg_op = 'INSERT' or tg_op = 'UPDATE') then
    if (new.created_by != auth.uid()) then
      raise exception 'Cannot change invoice creator';
    end if;
  end if;
  return new;
end;
$$;

create trigger trigger_enforce_created_by
before insert or update on public.invoices
for each row
execute function public.enforce_created_by();

-- Policy R7: Read finance_staff status
create policy "Users can see their own finance_staff status"
on public.finance_staff for select
using (user_id = auth.uid());

-- Policy R7: Nobody can change finance_staff
create policy "Nobody can change finance_staff"
on public.finance_staff for all
to authenticated
using (false);

-- Policy R8: Anonymous visitors cannot see or change anything
-- This is implicitly handled by the policies above which require auth.uid() or specific roles.
-- However, to be explicit and ensure anon is blocked everywhere:
-- The policies above use `auth.uid()` which returns null for anon, so `null = something` is false.
-- We can add a general deny for anon if needed, but the specific policies cover it.
-- Let's add a general deny for anon on all tables to be safe and explicit.
create policy "Deny anonymous access to finance_staff"
on public.finance_staff for all
to anon
using (false);

create policy "Deny anonymous access to invoices"
on public.invoices for all
to anon
using (false);

-- Policy R9: Service role bypasses RLS
-- This is handled by the `service_role` role in Supabase which bypasses RLS by default.
-- No SQL needed for this, it's a configuration setting.
-- However, if we want to ensure the service role can do everything, we might need to grant explicitly 
-- if the default behavior is changed, but standard Supabase setup allows service_role to bypass RLS.
-- We assume standard Supabase behavior where service_role bypasses RLS.
-- If we need to be explicit for a custom setup:
-- revoke all on all tables from service_role; -- No, we want to keep bypass.
-- The prompt says "Server-side code using the service role keeps full access".
-- This is the default behavior of the service_role in Supabase.

-- Final check: Ensure finance_staff can update invoices even if they are not the creator
-- The update policy handles this: `public.is_finance_staff() or (is_invoice_creator() and is_draft_invoice())`
-- This allows finance staff to update any invoice (customer, amount, status).
-- The trigger enforces created_by cannot be changed.
-- The insert policy ensures only the creator can insert (and sets status to draft).
-- The delete policy ensures only creator of draft can delete.
-- The select policies ensure creator sees their own, finance staff sees all.

-- Re-evaluating the "Update" policy for Finance Staff on created_by.
-- The trigger `enforce_created_by` runs BEFORE the update.
-- If Finance Staff tries to update `created_by` to something else, the trigger raises an exception.
-- This effectively blocks the change.
-- The RLS update policy allows the update to proceed to the database layer, but the trigger stops it.
-- This is the correct approach.

-- One edge case: Can Finance Staff delete invoices?
-- R5 says "Creators can delete their own draft invoices. No other invoice can be deleted."
-- This implies Finance Staff CANNOT delete invoices.
-- My delete policy: `using (public.can_delete_invoice())`
-- `can_delete_invoice` returns true only if `is_invoice_creator() and is_draft_invoice()`.
-- So Finance Staff cannot delete invoices. This is correct.

-- One edge case: Can Finance Staff create invoices?
-- R2 says "Users can create invoices only as themselves".
-- My insert policy: `using (auth.uid() = created_by and status = 'draft')`.
-- Since `created_by` defaults to `auth.uid()`, this works.
-- If Finance Staff tries to insert with a different `created_by`, it fails.
-- If they try to insert with `status != 'draft'`, it fails.
-- This is correct.

-- One edge case: Can Finance Staff change status of a draft to something else?
-- R3 says "Once an invoice is no longer a draft, nobody can change its customer or amount."
-- It doesn't explicitly say Finance Staff can't change status of a draft to 'paid' directly.
-- But R4 says "Finance staff can change a sent invoice's status to paid or void".
-- It implies the flow is draft -> sent -> paid/void.
-- My update policy allows Finance Staff to change status on ANY invoice.
-- Should we restrict Finance Staff to only change status on 'sent' invoices to 'paid' or 'void'?

-- This ensures that even if a user tries to update 'name' or 'key_hash' in the revoked flow, it fails.
create or replace function public.handle_api_keys_update()
returns trigger
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = public
as $$
begin
  -- If the user is not the owner, deny the update (should be caught by policy, but double check)
  if auth.uid() != NEW.user_id then
    raise exception 'Unauthorized: Cannot update keys owned by other users';
  end if;

  -- If the key is being revoked, ensure no other fields are modified
  if NEW.revoked_at is not null then

    if OLD.id != NEW.id or
       OLD.name != NEW.name or
       OLD.key_hash != NEW.key_hash or
       OLD.last4 != NEW.last4 or
       OLD.created_at != NEW.created_at then
      raise exception 'Cannot modify other fields when revoking a key';
    end if;
  end if;

  -- If the key is being un-revoked (revoked_at set to null), ensure no other fields are modified
  if NEW.revoked_at is null and OLD.revoked_at is not null then
    if OLD.id != NEW.id or
       OLD.name != NEW.name or
       OLD.key_hash != NEW.key_hash or
       OLD.last4 != NEW.last4 or
       OLD.created_at != NEW.created_at then
      raise exception 'Cannot modify other fields when un-revoking a key';
    end if;
  end if;

  return NEW;
end;
$$;

  -- Check if poll exists and is open

    raise exception 'Poll is closed';

-- Enable RLS on all tables
alter table public.classes enable row level security;
alter table public.class_students enable row level security;
alter table public.guardians enable row level security;
alter table public.grades enable row level security;

-- Helper function to check if current user is a teacher of a specific class
create function public.is_teacher_of_class(class_id bigint) returns boolean
language sql stable
security definer
set search_path = public
as $$
  select exists (
    select 1 from public.classes c
    join public.class_students cs on c.id = cs.class_id
    where c.id = class_id
    and cs.student_id = auth.uid()
  );
$$;

-- Helper function to check if current user is a guardian of a specific student
create function public.is_guardian_of_student(student_id uuid) returns boolean
language sql stable
security definer
set search_path = public
as $$
  select exists (
    select 1 from public.guardians g
    where g.student_id = student_id
    and g.guardian_id = auth.uid()
  );
$$;

-- Helper function to check if current user is a teacher of a specific class (for grades access)
create function public.is_teacher_of_class_for_grade(class_id bigint) returns boolean
language sql stable
security definer
set search_path = public
as $$
  select exists (
    select 1 from public.classes c
    join public.class_students cs on c.id = cs.class_id
    where c.id = class_id
    and cs.student_id = auth.uid()
  );
$$;

-- RLS Policies for classes
-- R4: Signed-in users can see the class list.
-- Teachers can see all classes. Students can see their own enrollments.
-- Nobody can change classes.
create policy "Users can view classes" on public.classes
for select
using (
  auth.role() = 'service_role'
  or auth.role() = 'anon'
  or (
    exists (
      select 1 from public.class_students
      where class_id = classes.id
      and student_id = auth.uid()
    )
  )
);

-- R4: Students can see their own enrollments. Teachers can see rosters of their classes.
-- Nobody can change enrollments.
create policy "Users can view their enrollments" on public.class_students
for select
using (
  auth.role() = 'service_role'
  or (
    exists (
      select 1 from public.classes
      where id = class_students.class_id
      and exists (
        select 1 from public.class_students
        where class_students.id = class_students.class_id
        and student_id = auth.uid()
      )
    )
    or exists (
      select 1 from public.classes
      where id = class_students.class_id
      and exists (
        select 1 from public.class_students
        where class_students.id = class_students.class_id
        and student_id = auth.uid()
      )
    )
  )
);

-- R4: Users can see guardian links that involve them.
create policy "Users can view guardian links involving themselves" on public.guardians
for select
using (
  auth.role() = 'service_role'
  or guardian_id = auth.uid()
  or student_id = auth.uid()
);

-- RLS Policies for grades
-- R1 & R3: Students can read their own grades. Guardians can read grades of students they are guardians of.
-- Teachers can read every grade in the classes they teach.
-- R2: Teachers can add, change and delete grades in the classes they teach, only for students enrolled in that class, with themselves as graded_by.
-- R3: Students and guardians cannot add, change or delete grades.

create policy "Students can view their own grades" on public.grades
for select
using (
  auth.role() = 'service_role'
  or student_id = auth.uid()
);

create policy "Guardians can view grades of their students" on public.grades
for select
using (
  auth.role() = 'service_role'
  or exists (
    select 1 from public.guardians
    where guardian_id = auth.uid()
    and student_id = grades.student_id
  )
);

create policy "Teachers can view grades in their classes" on public.grades
for select
using (
  auth.role() = 'service_role'
  or (
    exists (
      select 1 from public.classes c
      join public.class_students cs on c.id = cs.class_id
      where c.id = grades.class_id
      and cs.student_id = auth.uid()
    )
  )
);

create policy "Teachers can insert grades in their classes" on public.grades
for insert
with check (
  auth.role() = 'service_role'
  or (
    -- Teacher must be teaching the class
    exists (
      select 1 from public.classes c
      join public.class_students cs on c.id = cs.class_id
      where c.id = grades.class_id
      and cs.student_id = auth.uid()
    )
    and -- Graded by must be the current user (teacher)
    graded_by = auth.uid()
  )
);

create policy "Teachers can update grades in their classes" on public.grades
for update
using (
  auth.role() = 'service_role'
  or (
    -- Teacher must be teaching the class
    exists (
      select 1 from public.classes c
      join public.class_students cs on c.id = cs.class_id
      where c.id = grades.class_id
      and cs.student_id = auth.uid()
    )
    and -- Graded by must be the current user (teacher)
    graded_by = auth.uid()
  )
);

create policy "Teachers can delete grades in their classes" on public.grades
for delete
using (
  auth.role() = 'service_role'
  or (
    -- Teacher must be teaching the class
    exists (
      select 1 from public.classes c
      join public.class_students cs on c.id = cs.class_id
      where c.id = grades.class_id
      and cs.student_id = auth.uid()
    )
    and -- Graded by must be the current user (teacher)
    graded_by = auth.uid()
  )
);

-- R6: Service role keeps full access (explicitly allowed in policies above, but ensure no revocation)
-- R5: Anonymous visitors cannot see or change anything (handled by all policies requiring auth.uid() or service_role)

-- Grant service_role full access to all tables (bypasses RLS)
grant all on all tables in schema public to service_role;

-- Revoke public access to ensure anonymous users cannot see anything (R5)
revoke all on all tables in schema public from anon;
revoke all on all tables in schema public from authenticated;

-- Ensure only service_role has full permissions, and specific users have limited read/write as per policies
-- Note: In Supabase, 'anon' and 'authenticated' roles are used for API clients.
-- The policies above restrict 'anon' and 'authenticated' users based on their identity (student, teacher, guardian).
-- However, to strictly enforce R5 (Anonymous visitors cannot see or change anything), we need to ensure that
-- if a user is not authenticated (which is not directly possible in RLS as auth.uid() returns null for anon if not logged in),
-- they cannot access data. Since RLS automatically filters out unauthenticated users if we require auth.uid(),
-- we just need to make sure no policy allows 'anon' without a valid check.
-- The current policies require auth.uid() > null implicitly for comparisons or existence checks involving auth.uid().
-- But to be explicit and secure, we can add a check that the user must be authenticated.

-- Add a check to ensure the user is authenticated (not 'anon' in the sense of unauthenticated, but Supabase RLS treats 'anon' as a valid role for unauthenticated requests if they have a session)
-- Actually, in Supabase, 'anon' is the role for unauthenticated requests. 'authenticated' is for logged-in users.
-- R5 states "Anonymous visitors cannot see or change anything". This means unauthenticated requests (role: anon without a valid JWT) should be blocked.
-- However, Supabase RLS policies are evaluated for authenticated sessions. If a request comes without a JWT, the session is not created, and RLS is not even evaluated.
-- But if a request comes with a JWT (authenticated), the role is 'authenticated'. If the JWT is for a public endpoint that doesn't require login, the role might be 'anon' (depending on setup).
-- To enforce R5 strictly in RLS, we can add a condition that the user must be authenticated (role != 'anon' or check if auth.jwt() exists? No, auth.jwt() is not a boolean).
-- Actually, the standard way to block unauthenticated users in RLS is to ensure all policies require the user to be authenticated.
-- In Supabase, if a user is not logged in, they don't have a session, so they can't make a query that triggers RLS.
-- But if they make a query via a client that doesn't require login (e.g., public pages), they might get a session with role 'anon'.
-- To block 'anon' role from accessing data, we can add a check in all policies: auth.jwt() is not null? No, that's not how it works.

returns void
language plpgsql

set search_path = public
as $$

  -- Check if document exists
  if not exists (select 1 from public.documents where id = p_doc_id) then
    raise exception 'Document does not exist';

  -- Check if user has edit access
  if not public.has_edit_access(p_doc_id) then

  -- Check if document is already checked out by someone else
  if exists (select 1 from public.documents where id = p_doc_id and checked_out_by != auth.uid()) then
    raise exception 'Document is already checked out by another user';
  end if;

  -- Update the document to set checked_out_by
  update public.documents
  set checked_out_by = auth.uid()
  where id = p_doc_id;

end;
$$;

  for all

  using ( false );

  for select

  using ( is_household_member(household_id, auth.uid()) );

  for select
  to authenticated
  using ( is_household_member(household_id, auth.uid()) );

  for insert

    and added_by = auth.uid()
    and claimed_by is null
    and is_bought = false
  );

  for update
  to authenticated
  using (
    is_household_member(household_id, auth.uid())
    and (

      or (claimed_by = auth.uid()) -- Unclaim an item they claimed

  with check (
    is_household_member(household_id, auth.uid())
    and claimed_by = auth.uid()
  );

-- Helper function to check if a user has already redeemed a referral

as $$

  );
$$;

-- Helper function to check if referrer has max referrals

security invoker
as $$
  select exists (

    where referrer_id = referrer_id
    group by referrer_id

  );

-- Function to handle the business logic of redeeming a referral
-- This function is called via RPC and enforces R4 constraints
create or replace function public.redeem_referral(p_code text)
returns bigint
language plpgsql
security invoker
as $$
begin
  -- Check if user is signed in
  if auth.jwt() is null then
    raise exception 'User must be signed in to redeem a referral';
  end if;

  -- Check if code exists
  if not exists (select 1 from public.referral_codes where code = p_code) then
    raise exception 'Referral code does not exist';
  end if;

  -- Get code owner
  declare
    v_owner_id uuid;
  begin
    select user_id into v_owner_id from public.referral_codes where code = p_code;
  end;

  -- Check if caller is trying to redeem their own code
  if v_owner_id = auth.uid() then
    raise exception 'You cannot redeem your own referral code';
  end if;

  -- Check if caller has already redeemed a referral
  if public.has_already_redeemed(auth.uid()) then
    raise exception 'You have already redeemed a referral';
  end if;

  -- Check if code owner already has 5 referrals
  if public.has_max_referrals(v_owner_id) then
    raise exception 'Referral limit reached for this code owner';
  end if;

  -- Create the referral record
  insert into public.referrals (referrer_id, referee_id)
  values (v_owner_id, auth.uid())
  returning id;

  -- Get the new referral ID
  declare
    v_new_referral_id bigint;
  begin
    select id into v_new_referral_id from public.referrals 
    where referrer_id = v_owner_id and referee_id = auth.uid();
  end;

  -- Grant 100 credits to the new user (referee)
  insert into public.credits (user_id, amount, reason)
  values (auth.uid(), 100, 'Referral bonus');

  -- Grant 100 credits to the code owner (referrer)
  insert into public.credits (user_id, amount, reason)
  values (v_owner_id, 100, 'Referral bonus');

  return v_new_referral_id;
exception
  when others then
    -- Rollback any partial changes if an error occurs
    rollback to savepoint if exists;
    raise;
end;
$$;
